topics.topic: Required operation result for the loser of a concurrent duplicate-active-record race
questions: What failure may the owning operation rely on receiving from storage when a second active record loses the race?

When two administrators concurrently create an assignment or grant for the same pair with no active record, which operation results are required: must exactly one succeed and the other receive the active-duplicate refusal, may the loser receive a generic concurrency/storage failure, or are multiple outcomes explicitly permitted provided exactly one active record remains?

judgement.why: P1 judged the same unchanged question about whether the concurrent duplicate-active loser receives the ordinary active-pair refusal or a distinguishable persistence failure.
options: Expose one duplicate-active conflict for both the operation check and a storage collision.
Expose AuthorizationRejected for the operation check but PersistenceError for a storage uniqueness collision.
Expose only an undifferentiated refusal in both cases.
consequences: The later contract chooses distinct failures: an ordinary duplicate is HTTP 403 and a raced storage collision is HTTP 500, while both preserve the single-active invariant and write nothing for the loser.

SqliteStaffAccessRepository.insert_staff_assignment: [FIELD_PROJECTION] MUST assert open state through the context and append every StaffProjectAssignment field with parameterized SQL and canonical serialization; a duplicate assignment_id, and a second assignment for a (staff_id, project_id) pair that already has one, MUST both surface as a translated persistence error rather than a silent overwrite.

SqliteViewerAccessRepository.insert_viewer_grant: [FIELD_PROJECTION] MUST assert open state through the context and append every ProjectViewerGrant field with parameterized SQL and canonical serialization; a duplicate grant_id, and a second grant for a (viewer_id, project_id) pair that already has one, MUST both surface as a translated persistence error rather than a silent overwrite.

SqliteServiceIdentityRepository.insert_producer_grant: [FIELD_PROJECTION] MUST assert open state through the context and append every ProducerProjectGrant field with parameterized SQL and canonical serialization; a duplicate grant_id, and a second grant for a (service_principal_id, project_id) pair that already has one, MUST both surface as a translated persistence error rather than a silent overwrite.
precedent.why: State 5 assigns AuthorizationRejected to an active duplicate found by the operation but requires a uniqueness collision at each SQLite insertion boundary to surface as translated PersistenceError, so sequential and concurrent duplicate attempts intentionally have distinct observable failures.
options: Expose one duplicate-active conflict for both the operation check and a storage collision.
Expose AuthorizationRejected for the operation check but PersistenceError for a storage uniqueness collision.
Expose only an undifferentiated refusal in both cases.
consequences: The later contract chooses distinct failures: an ordinary duplicate is HTTP 403 and a raced storage collision is HTTP 500, while both preserve the single-active invariant and write nothing for the loser.

topics.topic: Required scope and cycle count for the INV-009 revoke-and-grant history test
questions: How many completed revoke-and-grant cycles must the INV-009 required test perform to satisfy “several”?
How many revoke-and-grant cycles must the required test perform to satisfy “several,” and must this history test be shown independently for staff assignments, viewer grants, and producer grants?

quotes: - INV-009: at most one active record per (staff_id, project_id) assignment, per (viewer_id, project_id) grant and per (service_principal_id, project_id) grant; revoked records of the pair stay, and a new grant after revocation is a new record

- INV-009: at `assign_staff_project`, `grant_viewer_project` and `grant_producer_project`: a pair whose records are all revoked receives a new active record and every revoked one is unchanged; after several revoke-and-grant cycles of one pair, every earlier record is still stored as revoked and exactly one is active; a pair with an active record is refused and nothing changes; and the storage refuses a second active record for a pair inserted past that check, leaving the first active record and the history unchanged.
- Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-009 [witness: verification:service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal].
- Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-009 [witness: verification:viewer_access_sqlite_uow_client_portal].
- Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: INV-009 [witness: verification:staff_identity_uow_client_portal].
judgement.divergence: A verification author may accept two cycles or exercise only one pair type, while another requires at least three cycles at each named operation; the representative-only outcome leaves the required history unshown for two of the three pair types, and the unstated meaning of “several” makes acceptance of the same two-cycle test differ.
judgement.why: State 2 owns what an invariant witness must show, but its Required tests item neither gives a determinate cycle count nor expressly states whether the several-cycle history must be demonstrated at each of the three named operations.
options: At least two complete revoke-and-grant cycles for each of the three pair types.
At least three complete revoke-and-grant cycles for each of the three pair types.
Multiple cycles for one representative pair type and only single-cycle coverage for the other pair types.
consequences: Different Factory reviewers can accept or reject the same focused test, and representative-only coverage can leave required history preservation unshown for named operations.

witness.initial: One named staff/project, viewer/project, or service-principal/project pair has no active record and may be granted or assigned by an administrator.
events: A verification author creates, revokes, and recreates records for the pair through two completed revoke-and-grant cycles.
The author submits that focused test as satisfying INV-009.
A Factory verification reviewer evaluates whether the test demonstrates the required several-cycle history and whether equivalent history must be shown for all three named operations.
outcomes: The reviewer accepts two cycles for one representative pair type as sufficient.
The reviewer requires at least three cycles independently for staff assignments, viewer grants, and producer grants and rejects the test.
basis: - INV-009: at `assign_staff_project`, `grant_viewer_project` and `grant_producer_project`: a pair whose records are all revoked receives a new active record and every revoked one is unchanged; after several revoke-and-grant cycles of one pair, every earlier record is still stored as revoked and exactly one is active; a pair with an active record is refused and nothing changes; and the storage refuses a second active record for a pair inserted past that check, leaving the first active record and the history unchanged.

topics.topic: Whether refusing a duplicate assignment or grant must append a rejected audit record
questions: Does a refused duplicate assignment or grant append the rejected audit record required by M36, or does “nothing changes” prohibit that audit write?

quotes:
Every other refused operation
rolls its transaction back and writes no record.
judgement.why: A13 expressly limits rejected audit writes to the two named actions, so a refused duplicate assignment or grant rolls back and appends no audit record.
options: Append exactly one rejected audit record while leaving assignment or grant records unchanged.
Write no audit record and change no persisted state.
consequences: The duplicate refusal leaves both the assignment or grant records and the audit history unchanged.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
State 2: decide required results and constraints, including necessary refusal precedence; carry test mechanisms, exact contracts and deployment procedures to their owners.
